title: Neon Courier 3D
premise: A neon-styled 3D arcade game where a futuristic courier runner moves around a cyber grid to sync drop-offs with roaming courier NPCs and build a delivery score.
interaction_model: Real-time third-person/isometric movement using WASD on desktop or a virtual joystick on mobile, plus UI toggles for render quality and camera mode.
objective: Approach roaming NPC couriers to trigger proximity-based delivery syncs and increase the deliveries score in an endless free-play session.
progression: The game begins with a suit-color choice and start action, then progresses as an open-ended score chase with repeated NPC encounters, ambient feedback, and optional camera/quality adjustments rather than levels.
theme: Cyberpunk neon courier run across a glowing city-grid plaza.
mood: Upbeat, stylish, futuristic, arcade-like, and lightly social.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy casual browser arcade games, neon sci-fi presentation, simple movement loops, and mobile-friendly score-chasing experiences.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is a free-roam score-chasing courier/contact game built in a single HTML file with Three.js.
High confidence in the control model, HUD flow, score mechanic, and NPC proximity interaction.
Medium confidence in whether the fiction should be read as literal package delivery or social courier syncing/tagging, because both framings appear in the copy and feedback text.
High confidence that there are no win/lose conditions or level progression implemented in the current code.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-friendly browser game called "Neon Courier 3D" presented as a compact cyberpunk arcade experience in a glowing 3D city-grid plaza. The player controls a futuristic courier runner shown as a simple stylized 3D character with a glowing visor, backpack, boosters, and a pulsing ring underfoot. Before starting, show a polished neon start card with the title, a short arcade-delivery subtitle, and four selectable suit colors that only change the player’s appearance. When the player starts, switch to a HUD that shows a delivery score plus buttons to toggle visual quality and camera mode. The core gameplay loop should be free movement around a bounded square arena using WASD on desktop and a thumb-stick style virtual joystick on mobile. Populate the arena with about fifteen roaming courier NPCs that wander between random targets and have floating glowing markers so they are easy to spot. When the player moves close to an NPC, count it as a successful delivery sync or drop-off, increment the score, play upbeat success sounds, show a toast message and a celebratory animated overlay, and briefly display a chat bubble over that NPC with delivery-flavored text. Let NPCs become scoreable again after the player leaves their radius so the session can continue indefinitely as a score chase. Include a neon shader-style floor or glowing lane grid, atmospheric lights and fog, subtle object bobbing and pulsing emissive effects, looping background music, and responsive UI that remains touch-safe on phones. Offer two camera views: an isometric chase-like view and a higher top-down view. The overall tone should feel sleek, energetic, readable, and casual rather than difficult, with no combat, timer, or fail state.
